concepts.title: China: From Empire to Republic and Revolution
concepts.definition: China entered the modern age through opium wars, unequal treaties and the Taiping rebellion that weakened the Qing empire, the republic of 1911 under Sun Yat-sen, warlordism, the Japanese invasion, and finally the Communist revolution of 1949 under Mao Zedong.
concepts.key_idea: China's path shows a modern nation built after a century of humiliation, with the 1911 revolution ending two thousand years of empire.

concepts.title: Japan: Meiji Restoration and Modernisation
concepts.definition: Japan modernised rapidly after the Meiji restoration of 1868, which ended the shogunate, restored the emperor, and adopted western technology, administration and education, turning Japan into an industrial power that defeated China in 1894-95 and Russia in 1904-05.
concepts.key_idea: The Meiji reforms rebuilt Japan's institutions within decades, and its exports of silk and industrial goods powered a modern economy.

concepts.title: Militarism, War and Rebuilding in Japan; Ideas of Nation in China
concepts.definition: Japan's militarist governments drew the country into the Second World War, ending with atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and an American occupation that rebuilt Japan with a democratic constitution, while China's intellectuals debated science, democracy and nationhood through the May Fourth movement.
concepts.key_idea: The years between 1895 and 1950 show both countries choosing militarisation and revolution in different measures on their paths to modernity.
